summary.text: Chris Coons is the Democratic U.S. Senator from Delaware and won re-election on November 3, 2026. A Delaware lawyer and former manufacturing-company employee, he served on and then led New Castle County government before being elected to the U.S. Senate in 2010. He sits on the Appropriations, Foreign Relations, Judiciary, Small Business and Ethics committees.

paragraphs.text: Chris Coons was born in Greenwich, Connecticut, in 1963, and, according to his Senate website, was raised in Hockessin, Delaware.

He earned a bachelor's degree in chemistry and political science from Amherst College in 1985, spent a semester at the University of Nairobi in Kenya, and later received a master of arts in religion from Yale Divinity School and a J.D. from Yale Law School, both in 1992.

After college he worked with the South African Council of Churches in the anti-apartheid movement, and as a law student he founded the Delaware chapter of the national "I Have a Dream" Foundation, later launching and running its AmeriCorps program, according to his Senate website.
He then worked for the Delaware-based W.L. Gore & Associates before entering county government; Ballotpedia also describes him as a nonprofit executive and attorney.
Coons served as president of the New Castle County Council from 2001 to 2005 and as New Castle County Executive from 2005 to 2010.

He was elected to the U.S. Senate in 2010 and has served since. His Senate site lists committee service on Appropriations, Foreign Relations, Judiciary, Small Business and Entrepreneurship, and Ethics; he is Vice Chair of the Ethics Committee and the ranking Democrat on the Defense Appropriations subcommittee.

According to the same site, he was an ordained elder in the Presbyterian Church and is one of three senators with a divinity degree. He lives in Wilmington with his wife, Annie; they have three grown children.
During the campaign, he ran on his Senate record.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 63.6% of the vote to Mike Katz's 36.4%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
